To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inherent dynamics of a recurrent neural network with sufficiently many neurons and diverse connectivity can be used to perform real time computation on time varying input, that stable states are not necessary to give a stable output, that the transient dynamics of such recurrent neural networks can serve as universal analog memory, and that the transient dynamics can be used to compute in real time from current and past inputs a desired output that may depend on the input in a nonlinear way.

the transient dynamics of recurrent networks of integrate and fire units may serve as universal fading memory, and that the high dimensionality and heterogeneity of the transient dynamics of such recurrent neural networks is a key factor in the computational power of the system.

1) the transient dynamics of a sufficiently high dimensional dynamical neural system may serve as a universal analog fading memory; and that 2) the transient states of a high dimensional dynamical state may be transformed by read out neurons into stable target states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new paradigm for real time neural computation based on transient dynamics of recurrent neural circuits that is applicable to a wide range of tasks.
the question how a continuous stream from a rapidly changing real world environment can be processed in real time by a neural circuit that is composed of stereotypical elements.
the following fundamental questions: What is the computational power of real time computing?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liquid state machine provides a new computational model of how recurrent networks of integrate and fire type neurons can compute in real time from a continuous stream of input.
our work shows that the brain may not be a Turing machine, but a liquid state machine.

this work presents a new framework for real time computing based on transient states in recurrent neural networks that is applicable to many tasks and does not require the construction of neural circuits that are task specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it provides a framework for the design of neural circuits for real time computing that can serve as a basis for a new generation of neural network based robots and neurotechnologies.

it provides a new computational framework for real time processing in recurrent circuits of neurons, which is not based on the construction of neural circuits with specific attractor dynamics, but on generic circuits with transient dynamics and a large number of neurons.
we propose a new framework for real time computation in recurrent neural circuits based on the transient dynamics of a high dimensional nonlinear dynamical system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
real time computation on time varying input can be based on transient states and does not need stable internal states.

real time processing of complex time varying input may not require stable internal states in recurrent neural circuits, but can be based on the inherent transient dynamics in the high dimensional state space of the recurrent neural circuit.
recurrent neural circuits may be able to process information in real time, and to compute in real time, even in absence of stable states.
